clue.text: Coins a common name for a metal worker

blocks.note: silver is loose change, coins in general
Smith is the commonest surname in Britain

explanation.surface: Someone minting coins has picked a very ordinary name for a craftsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coins' looks like a verb (invents) but is a noun for money, here silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A silversmith is a craftsman who makes objects from precious metal, so a kind of metal worker.

clue.text: Modest type retiring to live abroad

indicators.note: abroad suggests being scattered widely, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: shrinking means shy, retiring
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A shy person is retreating to settle overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like stopping work; here it means bashful.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an exceedingly shy, self-effacing person, a modest type.

clue.text: Common language

blocks.note: surface reading: a shared tongue, a lingua franca
setter's reading: common in the sense of vulgar or informal speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'Common' suggests shared by all, but it also means ordinary or low, the register of slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingo is a casual or slangy word for a tongue or jargon, everyday speech.

clue.text: Viewer gives attention to dance

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it closely
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a dance attentively.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives attention to' reads like a verb joining viewer and dance, but it is the first piece of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The eyeball is the organ of sight, the part of the body that views.

clue.text: Good to be nastily disposed?

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so the letters are placed in a new order

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A wry question whether being ill-tempered can count as virtue.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the nastiest word rearranges into the holiest.
explanation.definitionFit: Saintly means very virtuous, like a saint, so good in the moral sense.

clue.text: Marks one gains in error

indicators.note: letters in error are in the wrong places and must be put right

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A teacher's marks show that one student got a better score by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' reads as one phrase, but 'in' is fodder and 'error' alone signals the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Insignia are badges or distinguishing emblems, identifying marks of rank or office.

clue.text: Superior form of learning

blocks.note: surface reading: a better or more refined style of study
setter's reading: superior as in higher in level, the stage of study after school

explanation.walkthrough: Superior suggests quality, but it simply means higher up, the tier of universities and colleges.
explanation.definitionFit: This term names university-level study, the tier above secondary schooling.

clue.text: Qualification awarded to Glaswegian, the lucky thing!

blocks.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree
someone from Glasgow is a Scot

explanation.surface: A Glasgow graduate is congratulated on a degree: lucky them!
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a figure or animal kept as a charm to bring good fortune.

clue.text: Street name changed to something flowery

indicators.note: changed means altered in form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A road is renamed to something prettier and more floral.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowery' looks like ornate language, but means belonging to a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: The stamen is the pollen-producing male organ of a blossom, a part of a plant in bloom.

clue.text: Fix up artist with selection

indicators.note: read upwards means taken back to front, an across clue borrowing a down-clue signal

blocks.note: RA is a Royal Academician
a range is a selection of goods

explanation.surface: An appeal to set up an artist with a choice of options.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix up' reads as one phrasal verb, but 'up' belongs to the wordplay, turning the artist round.
explanation.definitionFit: To fix something such as a meeting is to settle or organise it, a synonym.

clue.text: Understanding of popular view

blocks.note: something in is fashionable, popular
a sight is a view or spectacle

explanation.surface: A grasp of what the popular opinion is.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception or grasp of a matter, a synonym of understanding.

clue.text: Sort of letter son cannot have translated

indicators.note: a translated text is rendered into new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A father worries about a letter his son is not allowed to have translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters split into vowels and consonants, so a consonant is one sort of letter.

clue.text: Glow after good meal out

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of order or wrong, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: The warm contentment that follows a good dinner out.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleam is a faint or brief light, close in meaning to a glow.

clue.text: Mistake for some to let rip

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is used

blocks.note: runs across the end of let and the whole of rip

explanation.surface: Letting rip is a blunder for some people.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a stumble or slip, figuratively an error or blunder.

clue.text: This disc could be a hit!

definitions.text: This disc could be a hit!

blocks.clueFragment: This disc could be a hit!
blocks.note: surface reading: a record that might top the charts

blocks.clueFragment: This disc could be a hit!
blocks.note: setter's reading: a clay target flung into the air to be struck by a shotgun

explanation.walkthrough: Disc and hit point to pop music; the disc is instead the target in trap shooting, and a hit is a shot that breaks it.
explanation.definitionFit: In skeet and trap shooting the target is a small flying saucer of baked earth that marksmen try to shatter.

clue.text: Lose one's temper with team? Quite the reverse

blocks.note: to flip is to fly into a rage
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of losing their cool with the team, then has second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the reverse' sounds like a retort to the rest of the clue, but it defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The flip side is the opposite aspect of something, like the B-side of a record.

clue.text: Automatic rejection by one in a hundred is standard

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown back, so the word is read backwards
in places one item inside another

blocks.note: the Luger is a German semi-automatic pistol
a ton is slang for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A rule about an automatic rejection rate of one percent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Automatic' is a noun here, the name of a gun; the Luger turned round gives the first five letters, then I sits inside A TON.
explanation.definitionFit: Regulation as an adjective means standard or officially prescribed, as in regulation uniform.

clue.text: On reflection, gold with Chanel appears rather elaborate

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: or is gold in heraldry
Coco Chanel, the French fashion designer

explanation.surface: Looking in the mirror, a gold Chanel outfit seems rather over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo describes an ornate eighteenth-century style, now used for anything over-decorated.

clue.text: Hurt feelings at the first complaints heard

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of that word is kept
heard means we want what is spoken, not what is written

blocks.note: the opening letter of the
whinges are moans; the word said out loud is spelt this way

explanation.surface: Someone's feelings are hurt on first hearing the grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: To whinge is British slang for to whine or complain. 'Hurt feelings' reads as wounded pride but means physical pangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinges are sudden sharp pains, brief sensations of hurt.

clue.text: Revealed access to open air

blocks.note: a secret that is out has been revealed
a door gives access to a room

explanation.surface: A doorway has been uncovered leading outside.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'open air' as the attributive open-air, an adjective like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Outdoor means situated outside rather than in a building, as in the open air.

clue.text: Teacher of note taking nothing from our university

indicators.note: taking nothing away means a zero-shaped letter is removed from the next word

blocks.note: G is a musical note
nothing is zero, the letter O
taken as written
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A distinguished lecturer at our university is taking no notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A guru is a spiritual teacher in Hinduism, and by extension any revered mentor.

clue.text: A French class can be hard

blocks.note: un is French for a
a kind is a class or sort

explanation.surface: A French lesson can be tough going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class' looks like a lesson, but means a category.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard can mean harsh or unfeeling towards others, which is what unkind means.

clue.text: Start to panic at endless crime wave

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter
without an end, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: crime with its last letter removed
the opening letter of panic

explanation.surface: Someone begins to panic at a never-ending crime wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crime wave' reads as one phrase, but 'wave' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To crimp hair is to press it into small waves or curls, so a crimp is a wave.

clue.text: Not aware of being overshadowed?

blocks.note: first meaning: ignorant of the facts
second meaning, taken literally: sitting where no light falls

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second sense is the literal one: something overshadowed is in shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means uninformed, while the literal phrase means located without light, as in shade.

clue.text: Feel item encapsulates our best

indicators.note: encapsulates means the words hold the target inside them

blocks.note: spans the end of feel and the start of item

explanation.surface: A product somehow captures the finest we have.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best or most select members of a group, its pick.

clue.text: A student has to stick around to get a job

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the others

blocks.note: to cling is to stick fast
taken as written
L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A student must stay put to find employment.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or profession, so a job in the general sense.

clue.text: Love to hold down this point of view

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
to pinion someone is to pin their arms and restrain them

explanation.surface: A lover is told to keep this particular view under control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' as nil comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is the view a person holds on a matter, their standpoint.

clue.text: Does he operate in the forest?

definitions.text: Does he operate in the forest?

blocks.clueFragment: Does he operate in the forest?
blocks.note: surface reading: a doctor performing operations out in the woods

blocks.clueFragment: Does he operate in the forest?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a specialist whose patients are trunks and branches

explanation.walkthrough: 'Operate' suggests a hospital, but this specialist cuts back and repairs woody plants.
explanation.definitionFit: This arborist prunes, braces and removes damaged wood from timber growth, like a surgeon on a patient.
